answer: A durable agent economy roots trust in staked identity rather than free signups: each participant locks collateral that a spiral binds to one canonical operator, so every duplicate costs more than it can earn, reputation then flows like a dune - slow to build, hard to fake, quick to wash out burst-created clones - while peer attestations interlock into a jade; a sybil must corrupt the whole jade, not one coral, before any reward is released. Any detected collusion forfeits the bond, so the attack never pays.
